compiled_state.description:
## Observation

`show_ticket` always computes `inbound_deps` by byte-scanning every event file in the store (src/rebar/reducer/_inbound.py, lines 39-72). On a clone of the live store, 2026-10-29, that is 139,978 files and 609 MB read per call. Only CREATE, EDIT, LINK, UNLINK and SNAPSHOT events change deps or parent (src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py). Restricting the scan to those types read 13,258 files and 150.5 MB, and found all 15 confirmed inbound links for the 1 ticket tested.

Caveats:
- The scan trusts that the filename suffix matches the event type inside the file.
- Link targets are stored as written, so a link stored by alias is missed by an id byte scan. That gap exists in the current scan too; on the clone, 2 of 1,605 LINK targets are not canonical ids, and both are free text.

## Plan
1. Restrict the inbound scan to the relationship-bearing event types by filename suffix.
2. Add a test that puts a link in each relationship event type and checks each is still found, plus one where a COMMENT body names the target and must not produce a false candidate.
3. Compare the inbound_deps of a sample of live-store tickets before and after on a clone.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The scan opens only CREATE, EDIT, LINK, UNLINK and SNAPSHOT event files.
- [ ] inbound_deps is identical to the current code for at least 50 tickets sampled from a clone of the live store.

## File impact (expected)
- src/rebar/reducer/_inbound.py
